# Airtable billing overview

# How does Airtable bill customers and what type purchase options does Airtable offer?

* Airtable offers two distinct types of plans: Self-serve and sales-led plans.

  + Self-serve Team and Business plans include monthly and annual billing options and are billed per workspace, not per account.
  + Sales-led Business and Enterprise Scale plans billing is calculated differently. Reach out to our sales team for additional context and information.

# What is a self-serve plan?

* While Business plans can be purchased independently, we also offer a more personalized Business plan through our sales team. Contact them to find out if a sales-led plan might better support your team's needs.
* Business and Enterprise scale plans require private email domains, meaning domains like Gmail, Yahoo, etc, are ineligible when upgrading to either plan.

Self-serve plans are plans that include monthly and annual billing options—allowing you to manage billing directly through Airtable. Self-serve plans include:

# What is a sales-led plan?

* Airtable's Sales team sells and manages the Business and Enterprise Scale plans. Contact them to find out if either plan might better support your team's needs.
* Business and Enterprise scale plans require private email domains, meaning domains like Gmail, Yahoo, etc, are ineligible when upgrading to either plan.

Sales-led plans are built in collaboration with our sales team. The sales-led plans include:

* Business plans
* Enterprise Scale plans

# How are self-serve Business plans and sales-led Business plans different?

* Self-serve Business plans are available to all Airtable customers.
* Sales-led Business plans are personalized through our sales team and require private email domains; therefore, domains like Gmail, Yahoo, etc. are ineligible when upgrading.

# How are self-serve plans billed?

* Self-serve plans offer monthly and annual billing options, billed per workspace, not per account.

  + Team plan owners are billed for any workspace or base collaborators with Commenter or higher-level permissions.
  + Business plan are billed for any workspace or base collaborators with Editor or higher-level permissions.
* Self-serve plans allow customers to upgrade individual workspaces while simultaneously managing other workspaces on the Free plan.

# How are sales-led plans billed?

Billing for Enterprise Scale and Business plans is calculated differently. Reach out to our sales team for additional context and information.

# When am I charged for my plan?

* If you add a payment method for the first time, the charge occurs immediately.
* If you update your existing payment method, the charge occurs at the beginning of your next billing cycle.
* If you upgrade your plan type, the charge will be applied immediately.

# How do update or remove my workspace’s payment method?

To update the card or payment method on your workspace:

1. Open your [Airtable account overview](https://airtable.com/account).
2. Select the workspace you want to update under "Workspace settings".
3. Open the "Payment details" section.
4. Enter your new payment method and save it.

Once it saves, the "Payment details" section shows your updated payment method. If it still shows the previous one, the change didn't go through—try again.

Airtable accepts credit cards, debit cards, bank debits, ACH (U.S. customers only), Apple Pay, and Google Pay. For details on reviewing or removing a payment method, see our Invoices and receipts article.

Updating an existing payment method doesn't charge you right away. The new method is charged at the beginning of your next billing cycle.

# FAQs

I received a warning about exceeding usage limits and have upgraded. Why is the over-limits badge still showing?

Exceeding usage limit alerts can last up to 24-48 hours after taking the necessary steps. If you continue to experience overuse warnings, please check your Workspace settings page. The workspace settings will display the amount of data being used per base and help you identify the issue.

Can Airtable refund a previously billed payment method (Credit/debit card, etc.) and charge a different card or payment method?

No. Once your payment method is charged, we cannot issue a refund or re-charge a different payment method. To learn how to update your payment, check our Workspace settings article.

Can I switch a Team workspace plan on one workspace to be associated with another workspace?

No, this is not possible. To “switch” a workspace plan, you will want to downgrade the active Team workspace to the Free plan and then upgrade the other workspace to the Team plan.

Note that Business and Enterprise customers can have multiple workspaces associated with their organization’s plan. In this case, admins can manage which workspaces belong to their organization in their admin panel.

Are Airtable plans priced in USD for international customers?

Yes, all Airtable plans are billed in USD (United States Dollars) regardless of location. When paying with a credit card, debit card, or other payment method issued outside the United States, the bank or card provider will handle currency conversion.

Currency conversion is managed by the bank or payment provider, not Airtable. Conversion rates and any associated fees are determined by the financial institution and may vary. Check with the bank or card provider to understand the total cost, including conversion fees, before purchasing a plan.

For enterprise customers with specific regional billing needs, contact the Airtable Sales team to discuss available options.

Why do I keep receiving 'Update your payment information' emails even though my details are correct?

Some customers receive a recurring "[Action Required] Update your payment information" email even though their card, billing, and tax details are already correct and unchanged. This is separate from the declined-payment email you get when a charge actually fails.

To resolve the issue:

1. Open your Airtable account overview.
2. Select the workspace named in the email under "Workspace settings".
3. Open the "Payment details" section and re-save your existing card, even if nothing has changed.
4. If you have a VAT or tax ID on file, open your invoice/billing details and re-save it too.

What payment methods does Airtable accept?

Airtable cannot enter your payment information or manually charge your credit or debit card.

* Airtable accepts all major credit cards, bank debits, ACH (U.S customers only), Apple Pay, and Google Pay for self-serve plans.
* Business and Enterprise Scale accounts are billable via ACH/invoice.
* Credit cards with 3D Secure enabled are not compatible with Airtable’s payment processor.

What should I do if my credit card is declined?

When a payment fails and is later retried successfully, there may be two charges close together on your statement: \* one for the retried payment and one for your regular renewal.

When billable collaborators are added or removed during the same billing cycle, prorated collaborators' costs can appear on the same invoice as other charges. This doesn't mean you've been billed twice for the same period.

Check out our Resolving declined Airtable payments article to learn how to resolve a declined payment.

What happens if my Airtable payment is declined, and how do I resolve the issue?

Check out our Resolving declined Airtable payments article to learn how to resolve a declined payment.

Does Airtable billing support split payments?

No. Our payment system is set up to upload only one credit card at a time and does not support splitting payments.

If you are unable to pay for the plan upfront on an annual cadence, we offer a monthly plan. To change your plan from annually to monthly, please access your Workspace settings page and select the “Change billing plan” option.

What happens if I change my plan from monthly to annually or from annually to monthly?

* Monthly plan customers who switch to the annual plan will be automatically converted to the annual plan, but will not be invoiced for the entire year until the end of the current month. At that point, they will be charged for each billable collaborator for exactly 12 months—at the discounted rate for the annual billing plan.
* Annual plan customers who switch to the monthly plan will remain on the annual plan until the end of their current billing cycle. After your annual billing cycle ends, your plan will renew on a monthly cadence at the monthly rate.

How are workspaces charged after upgrading to a Business plan?

Business plans paid via credit card use the credit card assigned on the admin panel “Billing” page. If you upgrade to a Business plan, any individual workspaces migrated to the Business plan will not use any attached credit cards in those workspaces for future payments. This is because Free and Team plans operate on a per-workspace level, whereas Business plans can contain multiple workspaces.
